Job's Reply to Zopbar's Second Speech In the preceding speeches of the second round, which ends with this speech, the friends had devoted their speeches to depictions of the fate in store for the wicked. Job's response to Eliphaz was a mixture of attacks on his accusers and lament for his sufferings; his response to Bildad was focused completely on his suffering. Now responding to Zophar, Job at last takes up the substance of the three friends' speeches by stating boldly that the wicked do prosper, flatly contradicting their essential point and thereby raising the book's great moral question.
